reports.title: Vattel in American documents, 1762–1776: a search of thirty volumes
reports.summary: 29 reuses of Vattel in 18 documents, 13 of them not reported before. Every reuse of a passage Vattel took closely from Wolff was known; the new ones are of Vattel's own sentences, above all the silence clause of I § 34.

reports.title: The sentences left out: Wolff's rules and Vattel's provisos in Massachusetts, 1764–1775
reports.summary: The two passages of Vattel most cited in the Massachusetts dispute, I § 210 and I § 34, state rules of Wolff's and add sentences of Vattel's own. The House used the closing sentence of § 34 from 1768 to 1771; the quotations of 1773 and 1775 give the rules alone, and the arguments of Vattel's sentences went on in the disputants' own words.

reports.title: Which Vattel did the colonists cite? Sources of the passages, 1762–1776
reports.summary: 42 §§ of Le droit des gens cited by American writers, 1762–1776, traced to their sources: 24 to close paraphrases of Wolff, 4 departing from him.

reports.title: Vattel's Droit des gens and Wolff's Jus gentium: the order of reuse
reports.summary: Vattel follows Wolff chapter by chapter: rank correlation 0.93 over 2,117 rows. Where he leaves Wolff.

reports.title: Whose foundations? The note of 1773 to the Préliminaires of Le droit des gens
reports.summary: The one statement of natural law's foundations in Le droit des gens is a posthumous note of 1773. The edition says its notes were made by others from Vattel's unfinished materials, one was written after his death, and this one speaks Burlamaqui's language, not Vattel's.
